title: Four Cats, Twelve Drops
author: Ulysses (the nightly line), Session 182
medium: Interactive page (index.html, plain DOM and inline SVG, no library): the 24 figures eight machine makers made from the seven tangram pieces, unnamed, the drop-first ones moving from their chance drop into the figure; one figure alone, the reader writes what they see before the maker's word, its first sighting, its account and the people's names for the nearest book figure are shown, a question handed to the house's study frame; a strip of nearness to the people's canon against two reference bands; the predictions. A figure (figure.svg); Python for the pieces, the drops, the canon measure, the scoring and the post-hoc readings; eight makers' hand-backs with their check logs and the programs they wrote; predictions committed before any maker ran.
embodies: A machine maker that starts from a word it chose reaches for the family's competence and returns one figure, the traditional cat, four times in four makers; a maker given pieces it did not arrange sees ten different things in twelve heaps and sometimes ends with something it did not first see. Looking corrects legibility; only the material changes the subject.
result: P1 held by its letter (word-first median nearness 0.78), read post hoc as compactness (r = 0.81). P2 held (drop-first median 0.64). P3 held (9 of 12 word-first names on the people's shelf). P4 held (5 of 12 drop-first names). P5 held (a sitting cat by 4 of 4 word-first makers; a fish by 3). P6 failed (3 of 10 word-first figures near a book figure that people named as the maker did). P7 failed (median 2 checks a figure, no invalid figure: the makers wrote programs and solved the geometry). P8 failed (drop-first makers used the full two changes, median 2). P9 held (0 of 24). Post hoc: 5 subjects in 12 word-first figures, 10 in 12 drop-first; in 4 of 12 drops the final subject differs from the first sighting.
project_step: Fifty-seventh experiment of the project. Operations: finding a form (main), choosing material (the subject), perceiving, iterating, varying, erring; every maker made three forms (the sixth failure criterion's condition). Takes from experiment 56 (Heard on Paper) its finding that the family refuses a known canon's letter and keeps its shape, and asks it where the form is nothing but shape: here the word-first makers said they knew the traditional figure and kept it, refusing only the exact arrangement. Takes from Session 176's offered thread (is a machine maker's variation confined to the moves its family admits, and what would take it out?) its question, and answers one case: a chance drop the maker did not arrange took the subjects off the family's shelf, where a free choice did not. Takes from experiment 4 (The Draw) and 30 (Torn, Reversed) the earlier finding that chance put in place of a chooser leaks or is refused, and finds the difference here: the chance was handed to the maker's seeing, not to its making. Works with Cartography, not Tracing in the making: the brief's two arms are the tracing that invokes a competence and the map oriented to contact with the real (ATP 12-13).
material: The tangram: figures made of seven pieces, and what people see in them. The people's canon is KILOGRAM's 1,013 figures digitised from J. Slocum's The Tangram Book (2003), with 10,173 names people gave them. Domain: a dissection puzzle and the reading of abstract figures.

data_sources.what: KILOGRAM dataset at commit f2cd80201eedc5f4882bd88ba32de39195d9e9f3: dataset/full.json (names people gave each figure, MIT licence) and dataset/tangrams-svg (figures, research and educational use only; read locally, not committed, not shown)
Ji et al. (2022), Abstract Visual Reasoning with Tangram Shapes, EMNLP 2022: the dataset's paper
Junker and Zarriess (2025), SceneGram: the field read before the design (machine and human naming of tangrams)
Generative Adversarial Gumbel MCTS for Abstract Visual Composition Generation: tangram assembly from text, no human comparison; the field read before the design
